mainTopic: When the general ברכה of שהכל is used: on bread and wine, with changed wording, on foods not nourished by the ground, and on spoiled dates (נובלות)
overview: The amud opens by finishing the rule for tree fruit: if the stalk does not stay and grow fruit again, the ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה. Next, רב הונא and רבי יוחנן argue whether שהכל works after the fact for bread and wine. Each one shows that his view fits both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, who argued about changing the wording of a ברכה. The story of בנימין רעיא then shows that a short Aramaic ברכה that mentions God counts for the first ברכה of ברכת המזון, even with different wording. רב says a ברכה needs God's name, and רבי יוחנן says it also needs God's kingship. A new משנה teaches that foods not grown from the ground, and spoiled or unusual foods, get שהכל. אביי explains that mushrooms grow from the ground but are not nourished by it, so they get שהכל. The גמרא then defines נובלות and moves the dispute about them to נובלות תמרה in a משנה about דמאי. A second version of that discussion begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A plant whose stalk does not regrow gets the blessing for produce of the ground
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the earlier rule: if the stalk does not stay and grow fruit again after picking, the ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה, not בורא פרי העץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where, when you pick the fruit, the stalk does not stay and produce again, we do not say 'Who creates fruit of the tree.' We say 'Who creates fruit of the ground.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its definition of what counts as a 'tree' for ברכות. If the stalk does not stay to grow fruit again, the plant is not a tree, so its ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא said a plant whose stalk stays and grows fruit again gets בורא פרי העץ. This line gives the opposite side of that test. The test is about the plant's lasting stalk, not about how the fruit looks.

keyTerms.meaning: Stalk or branch of the plant
Produces again
The ברכה on fruit that grows on a tree
The ברכה on produce that grows from the ground

steps.whatToRemember: The test for a 'tree' is whether the stalk stays and grows fruit again after picking. If it does not, say בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule that decides between העץ and האדמה, for example on bananas, which are האדמה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּכִי שָׁקְלַתְּ לֵיהּ לְפֵירֵי
phrases.english: But where, when you take the fruit,
the stalk does not remain to produce again,
we do not bless on it 'Who creates fruit of the tree'
but rather 'Who creates fruit of the ground.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּכִי שָׁקְלַתְּ לֵיהּ לְפֵירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the tree-versus-ground definition begun on the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If the stalk does not regrow fruit after picking, the ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the general blessing works for everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that if someone said שהכל on any food, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And on all of them, if he said שהכל...' (he fulfilled his obligation).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the dispute in the next step about how far that line goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says שהכל works on 'all' foods. The open question is whether 'all' really includes bread and wine, which have their own special ברכות. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: The general ברכה: 'By whose word all things came to be'
And on all of them (all foods)
Etcetera (the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: And on all of them,
if he said 'By whose word all things...' etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying שהכל on any food fulfills the obligation.

steps.title: רב הונא and רבי יוחנן argue about bread and wine
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says שהכל works on everything except bread and wine. רבי יוחנן says it works even on bread and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב הונא said, except for bread and wine. And רבי יוחנן said, even bread and wine.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about how to read the משנה's word 'all.' רב הונא leaves out bread and wine, while רבי יוחנן includes them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread and wine have their own special ברכות, המוציא and בורא פרי הגפן. רב הונא thinks a general ברכה cannot replace those special ones. רבי יוחנן takes 'all' literally, so שהכל works even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
Except for
Bread and wine

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions are only about after the fact (בדיעבד). Nobody says you should plan to say שהכל on bread.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Huna said:
except for bread and wine.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
even bread and wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the משנה's rule reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: שהכל does not work for bread and wine. רבי יוחנן: it works even for them.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי on changing a ברכה's wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the dispute matches a ברייתא. There, רבי מאיר says a self-made praise over bread or a fig still counts, and רבי יוסי says changing the Sages' set wording does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים: If someone saw bread and said 'How nice is this bread, blessed is the One Who created it,' he fulfilled his obligation. If he saw a fig and said 'How nice is this fig, blessed is the One Who created it,' he fulfilled his obligation. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: anyone who changes the set form the Sages fixed for ברכות has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an older dispute between תנאים to see if it matches רב הונא and רבי יוחנן. This sets up the comparison in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is flexible: a ברכה in your own words still counts. רבי יוסי is strict: you must use the exact wording the Sages fixed. That looks like the same split as between רבי יוחנן and רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this matches a dispute of תנאים?
The Omnipresent (a name for God)
He fulfilled his obligation
The set form (literally 'coin') the Sages fixed

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוסי's rule about the 'coin' of the Sages is a key idea in all הלכות ברכות: the wording of a ברכה is fixed.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like a dispute of Tannaim:
If one saw bread and said:
'How pleasant is this bread,
blessed is the Omnipresent Who created it' — he fulfilled his obligation.
If one saw a fig and said
'How pleasant is this fig,
blessed is the Omnipresent Who created it' — he fulfilled his obligation;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Anyone who changes from the formula
that the Sages coined for blessings —
has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an older source that might line up with the dispute in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute between רב הונא and רבי יוחנן is really an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא) with רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי on changing the wording of a ברכה.

steps.title: Suggesting רב הונא follows רבי יוסי and רבי יוחנן follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests matching them up: רב הונא is like the strict רבי יוסי, and רבי יוחנן is like the flexible רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב הונא holds like רבי יוסי, and רבי יוחנן holds like רבי מאיר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the proposed match between the two pairs. It asks whether these אמוראים are just repeating the older argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this match were true, each אמורא would simply be taking a side in a dispute of תנאים. The גמרא usually prefers to show that an אמורא's view works for everyone. So the next step will try to break this match.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא often rejects)
In line with רבי יוסי

phrases.aramaic: נֵימָא רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Shall we say Rav Huna holds like Rabbi Yosei,
and Rabbi Yochanan holds like Rabbi Meir?!

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States outright the match suggested by the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute between the אמוראים just the same as the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי?

steps.title: רב הונא: even רבי מאיר needs bread to be mentioned
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says his view fits even רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר only allowed a changed ברכה when the word 'bread' was said. שהכל does not mention bread, so even רבי מאיר agrees it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can tell you: I said my rule even according to רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר only said it counts there, where the person mentions the name 'bread.' But where he does not mention 'bread,' even רבי מאיר agrees it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the match from step 5. רב הונא's strict view does not depend on agreeing with רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's case, the person said 'this bread,' so his praise still named the specific food. שהכל names nothing specific. So רבי מאיר's leniency does not reach שהכל on bread, and רב הונא fits everyone's view.

keyTerms.meaning: He can tell you (introduces a defense)
He only said this as far as... (limits a source)
Mentions its name
Agrees

steps.whatToRemember: The match of רב הונא to רבי יוסי is rejected. Even רבי מאיר requires that a changed ברכה still name the specific food. So רב הונא's view that שהכל does not work for bread fits רבי מאיר too.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר does not say any words at all work. He only allows changed wording when the specific food is still named.

phrases.english: Rav Huna can tell you:
I said it even according to Rabbi Meir;

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir only said there

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּקָא מַדְכַּר שְׁמֵיהּ דְּפַת,
phrases.english: where he mentions the name of bread,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלָא קָא מַדְכַּר שְׁמֵיהּ דְּפַת
phrases.english: but where he does not mention the name of bread,
even Rabbi Meir agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested match from step 5 by limiting רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רב הונא must hold like רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggested match ignored that in רבי מאיר's case the person still named 'bread.' שהכל does not name it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's view fits even רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says his view works even according to רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי only rejected a ברכה the Sages never set up. שהכל is a ברכה the Sages did set up, so even רבי יוסי agrees that it works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן could say to you: I said my view even according to רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי only ruled that way there because the person said a ברכה the Sages never set up. But if he said 'שהכל נהיה בדברו', which the Sages did set up, even רבי יוסי agrees that it counts.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as רב הונא showed his view fits רבי מאיר, now רבי יוחנן shows his view fits רבי יוסי. This means the dispute between רב הונא and רבי יוחנן does not depend on the ברייתא at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's objection is to a homemade ברכה that the Sages never created. שהכל is an official ברכה made by the Sages, even if it is not the usual ברכה for bread. So רבי יוסי has no problem with it, and רבי יוחנן's view fits him too.

keyTerms.meaning: I said my view even according to... (my view fits even this opinion)
he only said his ruling (in that specific case)
the Sages set up / instituted it
agrees

steps.whatToRemember: Both suggested matchups fail. רב הונא fits רבי מאיר, and רבי יוחנן fits רבי יוסי. Their dispute about שהכל on bread and wine stands apart from the ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי does not say every changed ברכה fails. He only rejects a ברכה the Sages never created. שהכל is still an official ברכה, even when it is said on bread.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan could say to you:
I said my view even according to Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei only stated his ruling there
because the person said
a blessing that the Sages did not institute;
but if he said 'by whose word all things came to be'
which the Sages did institute,
even Rabbi Yosei agrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לָךְ: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 6. רב הונא fit himself to רבי מאיר, and now רבי יוחנן fits himself to רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the second half of the matchup from step 5, which tied רבי יוחנן only to רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The matchup assumed רבי יוסי rejects any changed ברכה. In fact, he only rejects a ברכה the Sages never set up, and שהכל is one they did set up.

steps.title: בנימין רעיא's simple Aramaic ברכה
steps.stepSummary: בנימין רעיא ate bread and said in Aramaic, 'Blessed is the Master of this bread.' רב ruled that he was יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: בנימין the shepherd ate a meal of bread and said: 'Blessed is the Master of this bread.' רב said: he fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about a simple shepherd who made up his own short ברכה. רב rules that it counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of ברכות that do not follow the Sages' exact wording. Here the words are short, homemade, and in Aramaic, yet רב says it works. This ruling will now be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: shepherd
ate a meal of bread (literally, wrapped bread)
Blessed is the Master of
he fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: Binyamin the shepherd ate a meal of bread,
and said: 'Blessed is the Master of this bread.'
Rav said: He fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about ברכות that do not follow the standard wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב rules that a short, self-made Aramaic ברכה over bread counts.

steps.title: A blessing without God's name is not a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב using his own rule: a ברכה without God's name does not count. בנימין's words did not mention God's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב himself say: any ברכה that does not mention God's name is not a ברכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on רב from another statement of רב himself. It looks like רב is contradicting himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Master of this bread' does not include a name of God. According to רב's own rule, that should make it no ברכה at all. So how could רב say בנימין was יוצא?

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say? (introduces a contradiction)
mentioning God's name

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל בְּרָכָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ הַזְכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם
phrases.english: any blessing that does not contain mention of God's name
is not a blessing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that בנימין was יוצא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's ruling contradicts his own rule that a ברכה without God's name is not a ברכה.

steps.title: He did mention God: 'the Merciful One'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בנימין actually said 'Blessed is the Merciful One (רחמנא), Master of this bread.' That does include God's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'Blessed is רחמנא, Master of this bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the story. It explains that בנימין did mention God, using the Aramaic word רחמנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רחמנא counts as mentioning God's name. So רב's ruling no longer contradicts his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, an Aramaic name for God
he (actually) said

phrases.english: He actually said:
'Blessed is the Merciful One, Master of this bread.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר: בְּרִיךְ רַחֲמָנָא מָרֵיהּ דְּהַאי פִּיתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought בנימין did not mention God at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said רחמנא, which counts as God's name.

steps.title: ברכת המזון needs three blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: ברכת המזון requires three ברכות. How could one short sentence be enough?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we require three ברכות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second problem with רב's ruling. One line cannot replace all of ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with God's name included, בנימין said only one sentence. ברכת המזון has three required ברכות, so saying he was fully יוצא seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: but don't we require?
three blessings (of ברכת המזון)

phrases.english: But don't we require three blessings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question on רב's ruling, now that the God's-name question is answered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One sentence cannot cover the three required ברכות of ברכת המזון.

steps.title: רב meant only the first blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב's word יצא means he fulfilled only the first ברכה of ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does רב mean by 'he fulfilled'? He fulfilled the obligation of the first ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows what רב meant. בנימין covered only the first ברכה, and he still needs to say the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברכה is about God feeding us (הזן), which matches 'Master of this bread.' So רב was not saying one line covers all of ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: what does 'he fulfilled', which he said, mean?
the obligation of the first blessing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think you can skip ברכת המזון with one line. בנימין was יוצא only for the first ברכה.

phrases.english: What does 'he fulfilled', which Rav said, mean?
He fulfilled the obligation of the first blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of רב's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב meant he fulfilled all of ברכת המזון.
steps.terutzMaskana: He fulfilled only the first ברכה.

steps.title: What is the lesson of רב's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Now that רב's ruling is limited to the first ברכה, the גמרא asks what new lesson it teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רב teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what is new about רב's ruling. This question sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He mentioned God and covered only one ברכה, so the ruling might seem obvious. The גמרא wants to know the new point.

keyTerms.meaning: what is he teaching us? (what is new here?)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the purpose of the ruling once it has been narrowed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The new law that רב's ruling teaches.

steps.title: A blessing counts even in everyday language
steps.stepSummary: The lesson is that a ברכה counts even when it is said in everyday language (לשון חול), such as Aramaic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though he said it in an everyday language, it still counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the lesson of the story. You are יוצא even if you do not say the ברכה in לשון הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בנימין spoke plain Aramaic, not Hebrew. רב teaches that the language does not stop the ברכה from counting, as long as God's name and the main idea are there.

keyTerms.meaning: even though
everyday (non-holy) language

steps.whatToRemember: A ברכה can be said in any language. בנימין's Aramaic line, which included רחמנא, counts for the first ברכה of ברכת המזון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that ברכות do not have to be said in Hebrew. It also shows that a ברכה must mention God's name.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲמָרָהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן חוֹל.
phrases.english: Even though he said it in a secular language.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲמָרָהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן חוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling teaches that a ברכה said in everyday language still counts.

steps.title: A משנה already teaches that ברכת המזון may be said in any language
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the lesson from Step 14: a משנה in סוטה already lists ברכת המזון among things that may be said in any language.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this in a משנה: 'These may be said in any language: the portion of the סוטה, the confession of tithes (וידוי מעשר), קריאת שמע, תפלה, and ברכת המזון.' So what new thing did רב teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 14. If a משנה already says ברכת המזון may be said in any language, רב's ruling seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said רב teaches that a ברכה said in everyday language (לשון חול) still counts. But the משנה in סוטה already says this openly. The גמרא does not like a rabbi's ruling that only repeats a משנה, so it asks why רב needed to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned this (in a משנה)
In any language
The passage the כהן reads to a suspected wife (סוטה)
The declaration a farmer makes that he gave all his tithes properly

phrases.english: We already learned:
phrases.notes: This signals that a משנה already teaches the point.

phrases.english: And these may be said in any language:
the passage of the sota, the confession of tithes,
the reading of Shema, prayer, and Grace after Meals.
phrases.notes: ברכת המזון is on the list, so the language question already seems answered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב's ruling teaches that a ברכה in לשון חול counts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already says ברכת המזון may be said in any language, so רב's ruling would add nothing new.

steps.title: רב adds that even a different wording counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב was needed. Without him, we might think another language is fine only when it translates the exact Hebrew wording of the חכמים. רב teaches that even a different wording works.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: that rule only applies when he said it in everyday language using the same words the חכמים set up in לשון קודש. But if he did not say it with the same words the חכמים set up in לשון קודש, you might say it does not count. So רב teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב adds beyond the משנה. The משנה allows a translation, and רב allows even a new, simple wording like בנימין's short sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in סוטה only tells us that the language can change. We might still think the wording must match the official text of the חכמים. רב's case of בנימין רעיא teaches that, after the fact, a different wording also counts. So neither the language nor the exact wording holds back the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed (this teaching is not extra)
It would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken first thought)
The holy language, Hebrew
Just as the חכמים set it up (the official wording)
So it teaches us (the new point)

steps.confusionAlert: The new point is NOT about language. The משנה already covered language. רב's new point is about wording: you do not need the exact text of the חכמים.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה teaches that language does not stop a ברכה from counting. רב teaches that, after the fact, the exact wording does not stop it either, as long as it has God's name.

phrases.english: It was necessary:
it would have entered your mind to say,
this applies only where he said it in a secular language

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתַקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן בִּלְשׁוֹן קֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: just as the Rabbis instituted it in the holy tongue,
phrases.notes: That means the same wording, only translated.

phrases.english: but where he did not say it in the secular language

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתַקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן בִּלְשׁוֹן קֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: just as the Rabbis instituted it in the holy tongue,
phrases.notes: That means he changed the wording.

phrases.english: I would say no, it does not count.
So he teaches us that it does count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that רב adds a new point beyond the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Another language is allowed only if it keeps the exact official wording of the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the fact, even a different wording counts, as in בנימין רעיא's short sentence.

steps.title: What every blessing must contain: God's name, or also His kingship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now looks at רב's rule on its own terms. רב says a ברכה without God's name (הזכרת השם) is not a ברכה. רבי יוחנן says a ברכה without God's kingship (מלכות) is not a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רב said: Any ברכה that does not mention God's name is not a ברכה. And רבי יוחנן said: Any ברכה that does not mention God's kingship is not a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the basic rule behind the earlier discussion and shows that it is a dispute. רב requires God's name, and רבי יוחנן requires 'King of the world' as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא assumed God's name is the key part of a ברכה. Now we learn that רבי יוחנן adds a second requirement: מלכות, such as 'מלך העולם'. So for רבי יוחנן, a ברכה with God's name but no kingship is still missing something.

keyTerms.meaning: Now to the matter itself (returning to a statement quoted earlier)
Mentioning God's name
Mentioning God's kingship (for example, 'מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם')
It is not a ברכה (it does not count)

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute sets the basic form of every ברכה. In practice we follow רבי יוחנן, and so our ברכות contain both God's name and 'מלך העולם'.

phrases.english: The matter itself.
Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל בְּרָכָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ הַזְכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם —
phrases.english: any blessing that has no mention of God's name —
is not a blessing.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
any blessing that has no mention of God's kingship
is not a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב's basic rule, which was quoted in the challenge of Step 9, and shows it is disputed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a ברכה needs God's name. רבי יוחנן: a ברכה also needs God's kingship.

steps.title: אביי brings a proof for רב from וידוי מעשר
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב's view makes more sense. A ברייתא explains the words 'I did not forget' as 'I did not forget to mention Your name.' It says nothing about God's kingship.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It makes sense to follow רב, as we learned in a ברייתא: 'I did not go against Your commandments, and I did not forget.' 'I did not go against' means: I did not hold back from blessing You. 'And I did not forget' means: I did not forget to mention Your name in that blessing. But it does not mention kingship.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a proof that supports רב. The ברייתא lists God's name as the needed part of the ברכה and leaves out kingship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse comes from וידוי מעשר, the farmer's tithe declaration. The ברייתא reads it as being about the ברכה said when separating tithes. Because the ברייתא mentions only God's name and not מלכות, it suggests that the name alone is enough, which is רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense to follow רב
As it was taught in a ברייתא
I did not go against (Your commandments)
It does not teach (it is left out)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
it stands to reason like Rav,
as it was taught:
"I did not transgress Your commandments and I did not forget":
"I did not transgress" — means I did not hold back from blessing You,
"and I did not forget" — means I did not forget to mention Your name in it.
But kingship it does not mention.
phrases.notes: This is the heart of the proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's side of the dispute in Step 17
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that God's name alone is enough for a ברכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining 'ולא שכחתי' in וידוי מעשר as mentioning God's name, with no mention of kingship

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reads the ברייתא to include kingship
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן has a different version of the ברייתא. In his version, 'I did not forget' means: I did not forget to mention Your name and Your kingship.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן teaches the ברייתא this way: 'And I did not forget' means I did not forget to mention Your name and Your kingship in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside אביי's proof. רבי יוחנן's version of the ברייתא includes kingship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's proof depended on kingship being missing from the ברייתא. In רבי יוחנן's version, kingship is there. So the ברייתא no longer proves רב right, and it even fits רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches (he has this version of the ברייתא)
Your name and Your kingship

steps.whatToRemember: רב says a ברכה needs God's name. רבי יוחנן says it needs God's name and kingship. אביי's proof for רב is pushed aside, because רבי יוחנן's version of the ברייתא includes kingship.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan teaches it this way:
"and I did not forget" —
to mention Your name and Your kingship in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes aside אביי's proof in Step 18
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ברייתא is rejected. רב's view itself is not proven wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof depended on one version of the ברייתא. רבי יוחנן's version includes kingship.

steps.title: Foods not grown from the ground get שהכל
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. For food that does not grow from the ground, and also for vinegar, spoiled dates, and locusts, one says 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: For something that does not grow from the ground, one says 'שהכל נהיה בדברו' (by whose word all things came to be). For vinegar, for spoiled dates (נובלות), and for locusts (גובאי), one says 'שהכל נהיה בדברו'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It moves from the earlier discussion to the ברכה for foods that do not fit the usual ברכות on plants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Foods that do not grow from the ground (such as meat or milk) cannot get a ברכה on produce, so they get the general ברכה of שהכל. The משנה also gives שהכל to foods that are spoiled or unusual: vinegar is spoiled wine, נובלות are spoiled dates, and גובאי are locusts.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (a new section of the משנה begins)
The general ברכה: 'by whose word all things came to be'
Vinegar (wine that went sour)
Dates that spoiled or fell off before ripening
A kind of locust

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין גִּדּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: And over something whose growth is not from the ground
one says, "By whose word all things came to be."

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַחוֹמֶץ וְעַל הַנּוֹבְלוֹת וְעַל הַגּוֹבַאי,
phrases.english: Over vinegar, over spoiled dates, and over locusts,
one says, "By whose word all things came to be."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ וְעַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין גִּדּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Foods not grown from the ground, and vinegar, spoiled dates, and locusts, get שהכל נהיה בדברו.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: no ברכה over a food that comes from a curse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees. Any food that is a kind of 'curse' gets no ברכה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Anything that is a type of curse, one does not make a ברכה over it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה. He says spoiled or harmful foods should get no ברכה at all, not even שהכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar and spoiled dates come from food going bad, and locust swarms are a disaster. רבי יהודה says we do not praise God over something that comes from a curse. The first opinion says these are still food, so they get שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of curse (something that comes from damage or disaster)
One does not make a ברכה over it

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not say these foods are forbidden to eat. He only says they get no ברכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
anything that is a type of curse
one does not recite a blessing over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה about spoiled foods
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food that is a type of curse gets no ברכה at all.

steps.title: Many foods in front of you: which one gets the ברכה first?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a new case. When several kinds of food are in front of a person, רבי יהודה says to bless first on one of the שבעת המינים. The חכמים say he may bless on whichever he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were many kinds of food in front of him: רבי יהודה says, if one of the seven species is among them, he makes the ברכה on that one. The חכמים say he makes the ברכה on whichever one he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new question: the order of ברכות when there are several foods. רבי יהודה and the חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה gives the שבעת המינים priority because the Torah praises ארץ ישראל with them. The חכמים give no such priority, so the person's own preference decides.

keyTerms.meaning: Many kinds (of food)
The seven species that ארץ ישראל is praised for (wheat, barley, grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives, dates)
Whichever of them he wants

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument about which ברכה comes first is the starting point for the later discussion in the גמרא about the order of ברכות.

phrases.english: If there were many kinds of food before him,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
If among them there is one of the seven species,
he recites the blessing over it.
And the Sages say:
He recites the blessing over whichever of them he wants.
phrases.notes: The חכמים give no built-in priority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the same משנה, after the discussion of שהכל foods and רבי יהודה's view on 'cursed' foods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: bless first on one of the שבעת המינים. חכמים: bless on any food you choose.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists foods that get שהכל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that lists foods that get שהכל: meat, fish, dairy, eggs, spoiled foods, salt, brine, truffles, and mushrooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: on something that does not grow from the ground, like the meat of domestic animals, wild animals, birds, and fish, one says שהכל נהיה בדברו. On milk, eggs, and cheese, one says שהכל. On moldy bread, wine that went slightly sour, and a cooked dish that spoiled, one says שהכל. On salt, brine, truffles, and mushrooms, one says שהכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that explains the משנה's rule ('food that does not grow from the ground gets שהכל') with many examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list has three groups. The first is animal foods, which do not grow from the ground. The second is spoiled foods, which lose their normal ברכה. The third is salt, brine, and mushrooms, which are not ordinary plant foods. The mushrooms in this list will cause the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (opens a ברייתא)
'By whose word all things came to be' (the general ברכה)
That became moldy
That went slightly sour
Brine (salty liquid)
Truffles and mushrooms

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין גִּדּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: Over an item whose growth is not from the earth,
for example, meat of domestic animals, wild animals,
and birds and fish,
one says: 'By whose word all things came to be.'
Over milk and over eggs
and over cheese, one says 'שהכל.'
Over bread that became moldy,
and over wine that went slightly sour,
and over a cooked dish that spoiled,
one says 'שהכל.'
Over salt and over brine
and over truffles and mushrooms, one says 'שהכל.'
phrases.notes: This last item sets up the next question.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין גִּדּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא returns to the משנה's first rule (step 20) and expands it with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animal foods, dairy, eggs, spoiled foods, salt, brine, truffles, and mushrooms all get שהכל.

steps.title: Do mushrooms not grow from the ground?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim that mushrooms do not grow from the ground. A ברייתא about vows shows that mushrooms count as 'things that grow from the ground.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that truffles and mushrooms are not things that grow from the ground? But a ברייתא teaches: one who vows off 'fruits of the earth' is forbidden to eat fruits of the earth but may eat truffles and mushrooms. And if he said 'all things that grow from the ground are forbidden to me,' he is forbidden even truffles and mushrooms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. A ברייתא about נדרים treats mushrooms as things that grow from the ground, which seems to contradict our ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the vow ברייתא, a vow against 'everything that grows from the ground' includes mushrooms. So mushrooms are גידולי קרקע. How, then, can our ברייתא put them in the 'does not grow from the earth' group?

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (opens a challenge based on an inference)
Things that grow from the ground
But a ברייתא teaches... (introduces a contradicting source)
One who makes a vow (נדר)

steps.confusionAlert: In the vow ברייתא, 'fruits of the earth' does NOT include mushrooms, but 'things that grow from the ground' DOES. The challenge comes from the second phrase.

phrases.english: Is this to say that truffles and mushrooms
are not things that grow from the ground?
But it was taught: one who vows off fruits of the earth
is forbidden in fruits of the earth,
but permitted in truffles and mushrooms;
and if he said, 'All things that grow from the ground are forbidden to me,'
he is forbidden even in truffles and mushrooms.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דִּכְמֵהִין וּפִטְרִיּוֹת לָאו גִּדּוּלֵי קַרְקַע נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the last item in the ברייתא of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's placing of כמהין ופטריות among foods that do not grow from the ground.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about נדרים shows that mushrooms are included in 'גידולי קרקע,' so they do grow from the ground.

steps.title: אביי: mushrooms grow from the ground but are not fed by it
steps.stepSummary: אביי separates growing from nourishment. Mushrooms grow up out of the ground, but they do not draw their food from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: as far as growing, they grow from the ground. As far as nourishment, they do not draw nourishment from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by splitting 'growing from the ground' into two separate ideas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the vow, mushrooms count as גידולי קרקע because they physically come up from the ground. For ברכות, what matters is drawing nourishment from the soil, and mushrooms do not. So they get שהכל.

keyTerms.meaning: As far as growing, they grow
As far as nourishment, they do not draw nourishment
The ground (Aramaic)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the halachic reason mushrooms get שהכל and not בורא פרי האדמה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
As far as growing, they grow from the earth,
but as far as nourishment, they do not draw nourishment from the earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק) between growing from the ground and drawing nourishment from it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mushrooms either grow from the ground or they do not, so the two ברייתות contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mushrooms grow from the ground (so a vow on גידולי קרקע includes them), but they are not nourished by it (so their ברכה is שהכל).

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'growth,' not 'nourishment'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that our ברייתא's wording is about growth, not nourishment, so אביי's distinction does not fit its words.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches 'on something whose growth is not from the ground'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer from the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even according to אביי, mushrooms DO grow from the ground. Yet the ברייתא lists them under 'whose growth is not from the ground.' So the wording still seems to be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: But look... (introduces a challenge)
It teaches (refers to the wording of the source)

phrases.english: But it says: 'Over an item whose growth is not
from the earth'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין גִּדּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer (step 25) from the ברייתא's language (step 23).
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's distinction as applied to the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא speaks about 'growth,' and אביי admits mushrooms grow from the ground.

steps.title: Correct the ברייתא: 'does not draw nourishment from the ground'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of the ברייתא to 'something that does not draw nourishment from the ground,' which fits אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read the ברייתא this way: 'on something that does not draw nourishment from the ground.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by correcting the text of the ברייתא so it matches אביי's distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new wording, the rule for שהכל depends on nourishment, not growth. Mushrooms are not nourished by the soil, so they fit the list, and the contradiction is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Read it as / correct the text to say
Draws nourishment (literally 'nurses')

steps.whatToRemember: Mushrooms and truffles get שהכל because they are not nourished by the ground, even though they grow out of it. This is why the ברייתא is read as 'שאין יונק מן הארץ.'

phrases.english: Emend it: 'Over an item
that does not draw nourishment from the earth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנִי: עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין יוֹנֵק מִן הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 26 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's rule depends on growth from the ground.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's rule depends on nourishment from the ground, so mushrooms correctly get שהכל.

steps.title: What exactly are נובלות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's item נובלות and asks what the word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one says שהכל over נובלות. What are נובלות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up a word from the משנה and asks for its definition. This sets up the next step, where two אמוראים answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that נובלות get שהכל, the lowest, general ברכה. Before we can understand why, we need to know what kind of food this is. So the גמרא asks a plain definition question.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of dates of poor quality; the גמרא now asks exactly what kind
What is it? (Aramaic)

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] 'And over the novelot [one says שהכל]'
What are novelot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the mushroom discussion and moves to a new item from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of the word נובלות in the משנה.

steps.title: Two definitions: dates scorched by heat or dates knocked down by wind
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא and רבי אילעא disagree. One says נובלות are dates scorched by the heat, and the other says they are dates that fell because of the wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא and רבי אילעא disagree. One said: dates scorched by the heat. The other said: dates blown down by the wind.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers to the question of what נובלות are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scorched dates ripened too early from the heat and are clearly damaged. Wind-fallen dates simply fell off the tree, so they may not be damaged at all. This difference is what the next steps test.

keyTerms.meaning: Dates 'cooked' by the heat: scorched and ripened too early
Dates of the wind: dates the wind knocked off the tree
One said (we are not told which אמורא held which view)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us which אמורא said which view. 'חד אמר… וחד אמר' just means 'one said… and the other said.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Il'a [disagree about this].
One said: dates burned by the heat.
And one said: dates [that fell] from the wind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either dates scorched by heat (בושלי כמרא) or dates blown down by wind (תמרי דזיקא).

steps.title: Why would wind-fallen dates be called a 'kind of curse'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wind-fallen-dates view from רבי יהודה's words in the משנה. Scorched dates fit the phrase 'kind of curse,' but plain wind-fallen dates do not seem cursed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבי יהודה says that over anything that is a kind of curse, one does not make a ברכה. This makes sense for the one who said scorched dates, since that is why he calls them a kind of curse. But for the one who said wind-fallen dates, what is the curse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses a line from the משנה to attack the second definition of נובלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה calls the items in the list מין קללה, a kind of curse. Heat-scorched dates really are damaged, so the label fits. Dates that just fell in the wind can be perfectly good fruit, so the label seems wrong for them.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
A kind of curse: food that came about through damage or misfortune
It makes sense for this view… but for that view…? A standard pattern for a challenge

phrases.english: We learned [in the משנה]: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Anything that is a kind of curse,
one does not make a blessing over it.
It makes sense according to the one who said 'dates burned by the heat,'
that is why he calls it 'a kind of curse.'
But according to the one who said 'dates from the wind' —
what is the 'kind of curse'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second definition from step 29 against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that נובלות are תמרי דזיקא (wind-fallen dates).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה calls the list מין קללה. Wind-fallen dates are not damaged, so they cannot be called cursed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה meant the other items, not the נובלות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה's phrase 'kind of curse' refers to the other items in the משנה's list, not to the נובלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי יהודה was talking] about the rest [of the items].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the wind-fallen-dates view with one word: אשארא, 'on the rest.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists vinegar, נובלות, and locusts. Vinegar is spoiled wine and locusts are a plague, so those are truly 'curses.' רבי יהודה's label goes on those, so the wind-fallen dates are not called cursed.

keyTerms.meaning: On the rest: the statement applies to the other items

phrases.english: [It refers] to the rest.
phrases.notes: That is, to the vinegar and locusts in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a statement: the label applies only to some items in the list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's 'kind of curse' covers every item in the משנה, including נובלות.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Kind of curse' covers only the other items, vinegar and locusts. So נובלות can be plain wind-fallen dates.
steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, the wind-fallen-dates view survives. רבי יהודה's 'curse' label refers only to the other items in the list.

steps.title: Second version: good wind-fallen dates should get בורא פרי העץ
steps.stepSummary: Another version of the challenge: scorched dates explain why the ברכה is שהכל, but wind-fallen dates are normal fruit and should get בורא פרי העץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the challenge went like this: It makes sense for the one who said scorched dates, which is why we say שהכל on them. But for the one who said wind-fallen dates, should we say שהכל?! We should say בורא פרי העץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the challenge. This time it attacks the ברכה itself instead of רבי יהודה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ruling of שהכל fits damaged, scorched dates, which are no longer proper fruit. Dates that merely fell in the wind are still good fruit, so they should get the normal fruit ברכה. In this version, the escape of 'אשארא' does not help, because the question is about the main ruling itself. The next step answers it by moving the dispute elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces another version of the discussion
Who creates fruit of the tree: the ברכה on fruit
He ought to bless with…

steps.confusionAlert: איכא דאמרי is not a new question added after the first one. It is a different report of the same discussion, aimed at a different part of the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This version is stronger because it targets the actual ruling of שהכל, which applies to נובלות directly.

phrases.english: Some say [the challenge was]:
It makes sense according to the one who said 'dates burned by the heat,'
that is why we bless 'shehakol' over them.
But according to the one who said 'dates from the wind,'
[we say] 'shehakol'?!
He should bless 'Who creates fruit of the tree'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of the step 30 challenge. It targets the ברכה rather than the phrase מין קללה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that נובלות are תמרי דזיקא, measured against the משנה's ruling of שהכל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wind-fallen dates are normal fruit. Normal fruit gets בורא פרי העץ, so the משנה's שהכל does not fit this definition.

steps.title: Plain נובלות are agreed to be scorched dates; the argument is about נובלות תמרה
steps.stepSummary: Facing the difficulty with the ברכה, the גמרא now says that everyone agrees plain נובלות are heat-scorched dates. The dispute between רבי אילעא and רבי זירא is really about נובלות תמרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, about plain 'novelot,' everyone agrees that they are dates scorched by the heat. Where they argue is about 'novelot temara.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty from Step 32 by moving the argument somewhere else. Plain נובלות in our משנה are agreed to be scorched dates, and the disagreement only concerns the phrase נובלות תמרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scorched dates are poor-quality fruit, so שהכל makes sense, and now no one holds the wind-fallen view about our משנה. This removes the problem with the ברכה completely. The wind-fallen opinion survives, but it now applies only to a different phrase in a different משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that the גמרא is dropping its earlier assumption
Plain, unspecified (the word used without any added description)
Everyone agrees; no one disputes this
Dates scorched or 'cooked' by the heat
'Novelot of the date palm,' a separate phrase found in the laws of דמאי

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the dispute disappeared. It still exists. It has only been moved from plain נובלות (our ברכות משנה) to נובלות תמרה (a משנה in דמאי).

phrases.english: Rather, regarding plain 'novelot'
everyone agrees (no one disputes)
that they are dates scorched by the heat.
When they argue, it is about 'novelot temara.'
phrases.notes: Their argument is only about the wording with the extra word תמרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בְּנוֹבְלוֹת סְתָמָא כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 32 by moving the dispute away from our משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute to a different text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אילעא and רבי זירא argued about plain נובלות in our משנה, which caused the problem with the ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain נובלות are agreed to be scorched dates, so the ברכה is שהכל according to everyone. The dispute concerns only נובלות תמרה.

steps.title: The משנה in דמאי listing lenient fruits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in דמאי that contains the phrase נובלות תמרה. It is a list of low-quality fruits that are treated leniently when there is a doubt about whether they were tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: These are the lenient items in the laws of דמאי: שיתין, רימין, עוזרדין, בנות שוח, בנות שקמה, גופנין, נצפה, and נובלות תמרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the phrase נובלות תמרה actually appears. It is in a משנה about fruits we do not have to tithe when we are unsure whether they were already tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce bought from an עם הארץ is called דמאי and normally must be tithed out of doubt. These fruits are cheap and inferior, so the רבנן did not require tithing them in a case of doubt. This list is where the dispute from Step 33 lives, and it sets up the explanations and the challenge that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The lenient ones; items treated more lightly
Produce from an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed, so it is tithed out of doubt

steps.whyThisMatters: This list connects the meaning of a word in ברכות to a practical question of tithing in another מסכתא.

phrases.english: As we learned: the lenient items with regard to demai are:
shittin, rimin, and uzradin,
benot shuach and benot shikma,
gufnin, nitzpa, and novelot temara.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text where the phrase נובלות תמרה appears.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Certain inferior fruits are exempt from tithing when it is uncertain whether they were tithed (דמאי).

steps.title: Identifying the fruits on the דמאי list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains, one by one, what each fruit in the דמאי list is. Several of the explanations come from רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: שיתין: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן that they are a kind of fig. רימין are lote fruit. עוזרדין are crabapples. בנות שוח: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן that they are white figs. בנות שקמה: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן that they are sycamore figs. גופנין are the last grapes of the season. נצפה is the caper fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is defining the words in the list so we know what each fruit is. These are all cheap, low-quality fruits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item on the list is an inferior or wild-type fruit. That explains why the רבנן were lenient with them in a case of doubt. Seeing this pattern prepares us for the last item, נובלות תמרה, which is the one in dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often transmits teachings of רבי יוחנן
A type of figs
The last grapes left on the vine at the end of the season
The fruit of the caper bush

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיתִין, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: Shittin: Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said: a type of figs.
Rimin are lote fruit. Uzradin are crabapples.

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹת שׁוּחַ, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: Benot shuach: Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said: white figs.

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹת שִׁקְמָה, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: Benot shikma: Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said: sycamore figs.
Gufnin are the last grapes of the vine.
Nitzpa is the caper fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁיתִין, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the items in the משנה quoted in Step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each item on the דמאי list is identified as a specific low-quality fruit.

steps.title: The dispute placed on נובלות תמרה
steps.stepSummary: Reaching the last item, the גמרא places the dispute of רבי אילעא and רבי זירא here. One says scorched dates, and the other says wind-fallen dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: נובלות תמרה: רבי אילעא and רבי זירא disagree. One says they are dates scorched by the heat, and the other says they are dates knocked down by the wind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same two opinions from Step 29. This time they are attached to נובלות תמרה in the דמאי list, as Step 33 said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not just a repeat. The dispute now sits in a new place, which allows a new kind of challenge, one based on the laws of tithing instead of ברכות. It sets up the קשיא that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Dates of the wind; dates blown down by the wind
One said... and one said (a dispute where we do not know who holds which view)

phrases.aramaic: נוֹבְלוֹת תְּמָרָה — רַבִּי אִילְעָא וְרַבִּי זֵירָא,
phrases.english: Novelot temara: Rabbi Il'a and Rabbi Zeira disagree.
One said: dates scorched by the heat.
And one said: dates knocked down by the wind.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹבְלוֹת תְּמָרָה — רַבִּי אִילְעָא וְרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of definitions with the item that is in dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether נובלות תמרה are heat-scorched dates or wind-fallen dates.

steps.title: Wind-fallen dates are ownerless, so why would certainly-untithed ones need tithing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wind-fallen view. The משנה implies that נובלות תמרה are exempt only in a case of doubt and must be tithed when we know they were not tithed. But wind-fallen dates are הפקר, and ownerless produce never needs מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says they are heat-scorched dates. That is why the משנה calls them 'lenient in דמאי': only doubtful ones are exempt, but definitely untithed ones must be tithed. But for the one who says they are wind-fallen dates, would definitely untithed ones need tithing? They are ownerless!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wind-fallen opinion. It reads the משנה closely: 'lenient in דמאי' implies that when there is no doubt, tithing is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scorched dates still belong to their owner, so they normally need מעשר, and only the doubtful case is exempt. Wind-fallen dates are left for anyone to take, so they are הפקר, and הפקר is fully exempt from מעשר. Then the משנה's limit to a case of doubt would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (opens a contrast between two views)
Those in doubt (whether they were tithed)
Those that are certain (definitely not tithed)
Ownerless property, which is exempt from מעשר

steps.confusionAlert: The proof comes from an implication. The משנה only says doubtful ones are lenient, which implies certain ones must be tithed. That implication is what clashes with the wind-fallen view.

phrases.english: It works well for the one who says 'dates scorched by the heat':
that is why it teaches 'the lenient items with regard to demai,'
meaning that it is the doubtful ones that are exempt,
but the definitely untithed ones are obligated.
But for the one who says 'dates knocked down by the wind':
would definitely untithed ones be obligated?! They are ownerless!
phrases.notes: Wind-fallen dates are abandoned by the owner, and ownerless produce is exempt from tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one side of the dispute just stated in Step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that נובלות תמרה are wind-fallen dates
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that certainly-untithed נובלות תמרה need tithing. Wind-fallen dates are הפקר, which is always exempt, so that implication cannot fit this view.

steps.title: The case is where the dates were gathered into a pile
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a person who collected the wind-fallen dates and made them into a pile, a גורן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where he made them into a pile, like a threshing-floor heap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the wind-fallen view by narrowing the case. It is talking about someone who gathered the fallen dates into a finished pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a גורן is the step that normally finishes the processing of produce and makes it ready for tithing. Once the dates were gathered and piled this way, they can become obligated in מעשר even though they started out as הפקר. The next step brings the source for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrowed case)
A threshing-floor pile; the finished heap of produce
That he made them into a pile

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing here?
Where he made them into a pile (like a threshing-floor heap).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 37.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wind-fallen dates are always הפקר and can never need מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: When someone gathers them into a גורן, they become obligated in מעשר. So only the doubtful ones are exempt.

steps.title: Source: gifts to the poor made into a pile become obligated in tithes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule. Gifts to the poor, which are normally exempt from מעשר, become obligated once they are made into a גורן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: לקט, שכחה, and פאה that a person made into a pile become fixed as obligated in מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that produce that is normally exempt from מעשר can become obligated once it is piled into a גורן. This proves the answer in Step 38.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לקט, שכחה, and פאה are like הפקר because they are free for the poor, and so they are normally exempt from מעשר. Even so, piling them into a גורן fixes an obligation of מעשר, which is a rule of the רבנן. In the same way, piled wind-fallen dates need tithing when certain, so the wind-fallen view fits the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose rule is quoted here
Gifts to the poor: fallen gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corners of the field
They became fixed (obligated) for tithing

steps.whatToRemember: Plain נובלות, the ones in our ברכות משנה, are agreed to be heat-scorched dates, so their ברכה is שהכל. The dispute is about נובלות תמרה in דמאי. Even the wind-fallen view works there, because ownerless produce that was gathered into a גורן becomes obligated in מעשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general principle: making produce into a גורן can create an obligation of מעשר even for produce that started out exempt, like הפקר or gifts to the poor.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov:
gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field
that one made into a pile became fixed as obligated in tithes.
phrases.notes: This obligation is rabbinic (מדרבנן), not from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source that supports the answer in Step 38.
steps.raayaObject: That gathered wind-fallen (ownerless) dates can become obligated in מעשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule that לקט, שכחה, and פאה made into a גורן become obligated in מעשר

steps.title: Opening a second version of the discussion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'some say' to introduce a different version of how the debate about נובלות תמרה went.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that the discussion went like this:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is telling us that a second version of the discussion about נובלות תמרה is about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version, in steps 36 to 39, challenged the wind-fallen dates view and answered with the case of a גורן. The words אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי mean that other scholars remembered the back-and-forth differently. Nothing is decided in this line itself. It only opens the alternate version, which continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There are those who say.' The standard formula for bringing a second version of a discussion.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'some say' as a new challenge or a new answer. It does not attack what came before. It only tells you that a different version of the same discussion is coming.

phrases.english: Some say (there are those who say):
phrases.notes: This starts a second version of the discussion we just finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first version of the debate ends at step 39, this line opens a second, parallel version of the same discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no ruling here. The line only signals that a different version of the discussion about נובלות תמרה follows.
